questions.question: A complete tool spec for the Claude API requires which three parts?
options: name, description, input_schema
name, examples, temperature
description, model, max_tokens
name, input_schema, tool_choice

questions.question: Claude is repeatedly calling the wrong tool out of two similarly-named tools in a set. Per the course's guidance on tool descriptions, what's the most direct fix?
options: Rewrite both descriptions to be more distinct about what each tool does, when to use it, and what it returns
Add a second Claude call that double-checks which tool was picked
Lower the temperature so tool selection is more deterministic
Add more few-shot examples of correct tool calls to the system prompt

questions.question: Two tools overlap in what they can do (e.g. one tool sets a reminder for 'a date' and another sets one for 'a duration from now'), and Claude picks the wrong one under time pressure. What's actually wrong here?
options: The tools have overlapping responsibility/granularity, not just unclear wording — they should be redesigned so each owns a distinct, non-overlapping job
Claude needs a few-shot example added showing the correct tool for each case
The descriptions need to be longer and more detailed
A verification pass should check which tool was called and retry if wrong

questions.question: What triggers a tool function to actually execute in the reminder-notebook project from this chapter?
options: Claude deciding, based on the tool's name/description and the user's request, that it needs the info/action the function provides
The developer manually calling the function whenever a tool_use block appears
A cron job polling for pending tool calls
The API automatically executing any registered function on every turn

questions.question: When Claude decides to use a tool, what does the assistant message actually contain?
options: Potentially multiple content blocks — e.g. a text block plus a tool_use block with the tool's id, name, and input
Only a single tool_use block, since Claude cannot emit text on a tool-call turn
A single plain-text string describing which tool to call
A tool_result block confirming the tool already ran

questions.question: Why does the developer need to preserve the full content-block structure (not just extracted text) when appending Claude's tool-use response to the message history?
options: Claude doesn't manage conversation history itself — the developer must resend the complete prior structure, including tool_use blocks, for the API to have full context
The API rejects any message history that contains plain text blocks
Tool_use blocks are automatically stripped by the API if not manually preserved, so this step is optional
It's only needed when using extended thinking

questions.question: After a tool function runs, how is its output returned to Claude in the next turn?
options: As a tool_result block referencing the original tool_use id
As a new system prompt describing the result
By re-sending the original user message with the result appended as plain text
Tool results are not sent back — Claude infers them from context

questions.question: What's the core limitation of Claude that tool use is designed to solve?
options: Claude's knowledge is limited to its training data, so it can't get real-time information or take actions in the world on its own
Claude cannot process JSON without a tool schema
Claude cannot hold a multi-turn conversation without tools
Claude requires tools to generate any structured output at all
